title.narrative: Aufstockung des Eigenkapitalbetrags der Côte dIvoire an der African Trade + Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI)
Increase in Côte dIvoires contribution to the capital of the African Trade + Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI)

description.narrative: Dieses Vorhaben leistet einen Beitrag zur Verbesserung der Rahmenbedingungen für private Investitionen sowie zur Schaffung von Arbeitsplätzen in der CIV.

The objective of the project is to contribute to increasing international trade and domestic and foreign investment in Côte dIvoire with a focus on the private sector. To this end, the project provides for a direct capital contribution to the African Trade + Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) to increase Côte dIvoires capital share. The African Trade + Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) is a pan-African insurance agency headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, over 85% owned and jointly managed by its member countries (from Africa, for Africa). ATI was founded in 2001 by seven East African countries with the support of the World Bank and the African Development Bank (AfDB). ATIDIs 33 shareholders currently include 21 African states and twelve institutional shareholders. ATIDI is registered with the United Nations as a multilateral organisation. Its mandate is to promote African countries (especially its member states) through trade and foreign direct investment by providing competitive insurance solutions for commercial and political risks, reinsurance and contract bond insurance. The direct target group of the project are national and international investors, banks/financial institutions and trading companies (policyholders). The indirect target group includes employees of investors, banks/financial institutions as well as trading companies, Ivorian (M)SMEs via financial intermediaries and their employees, who indirectly benefit from ATIDI-insured transactions, as well as their economic partners, e.g. through the creation of jobs, increase in purchasing power and improvement of the supply of goods and services, etc.

To this end, the project provides for a direct capital contribution to the African Trade + Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) to increase Côte dIvoires capital share. The African Trade + Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) is a pan-African insurance agency headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, over 85% owned and jointly managed by its member countries (from Africa, for Africa). ATI was founded in 2001 by seven East African countries with the support of the World Bank and the African Development Bank (AfDB). ATIDIs 33 shareholders currently include 21 African states and twelve institutional shareholders. ATIDI is registered with the United Nations as a multilateral organisation. Its mandate is to promote African countries (especially its member states) through trade and foreign direct investment by providing competitive insurance solutions for commercial and political risks, reinsurance and contract bond insurance. The direct target group of the project are national and international investors, banks/financial institutions and trading companies (policyholders). The indirect target group includes employees of investors, banks/financial institutions as well as trading companies, Ivorian (M)SMEs via financial intermediaries and their employees, who indirectly benefit from ATIDI-insured transactions, as well as their economic partners, e.g. through the creation of jobs, increase in purchasing power and improvement of the supply of goods and services, etc.

Ziel des Vorhabens ist es, einen Beitrag zur Steigerung von internationalem Handel und in- und ausländischen Investitionen in der Côte dIvoire mit Fokus auf den Privatsektor zu leisten. Dazu sieht das Vorhaben die direkte Kapitaleinzahlung in die African Trade + Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) zur Aufstockung der Kapitaleinlage Côte dIvoires vor. Die African Trade + Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) ist eine pan-afrikanische Versicherungsagentur mit Hauptsitz in Nairobi, Kenia, die zu über 85% ihren Mitgliedsländern gehört und von ihnen gemeinschaftlich verwaltet wird (aus Afrika, für Afrika). ATIDI wurde 2001 mit Unterstützung der Weltbank und der Afrikanischen Entwicklungsbank (AfDB) von sieben ostafrikanischen Ländern gegründet. Zu den mittlerweile 33 Gesellschaftern von ATIDI gehören aktuell 21 afrikanische Staaten und zwölf institutionelle Anteilseigner. ATIDI ist bei den Vereinten Nationen als multilaterale Organisation registriert. Ihr Mandat ist es, afrikanische Länder (insbesondere ihre Mitgliedsstaaten) durch Handel und ausländische Direktinvestitionen zu fördern, indem wettbewerbsfähige Versicherungslösungen für kommerzielle und politische Risiken, Rückversicherungen und Vertragsgarantieversicherungen angeboten werden. Die unmittelbare Zielgruppe des Vorhabens sind Investoren, Banken/Finanzinstitutionen sowie Handelsunternehmen aus dem In- und Ausland (Versicherungsnehmer). Zur mittelbaren Zielgruppe zählen Beschäftigte von Investoren, Banken/Finanzinstitutionen sowie Handelsunternehmen, ivorische (K)KMUs über Finanzintermediäre und deren Beschäftigte, die von ATIDI-versicherten Transaktionen indirekt profitieren sowie deren Wirtschaftspartner, z.B. durch die Schaffung von Arbeitsplätzen, Erhöhung der Kaufkraft und Verbesserung des Angebots an Waren und Dienstleistungen etc.
